newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Santos workers considering port authority proposal.
newsitem.headline: Santos workers considering port authority proposal.

text.p: Administrative portworkers at Brazil's key port of Santos were meeting to consider a proposal by port authority CODESP aimed at ending a strike at the port, a CODESP spokeswoman said.

The Administrative Portworkers' Union, which went on strike in the early hours, began an assembly at 1700 local/2000 GMT following talks with CODESP at the local division of the Labor Ministry, she said.
"CODESP's proposal was conditional on their returning to work," the spokeswoman said. "They are meeting now and we hope they will return to work."

The workers are protesting against not being consulted about the port's switch to 24-hour operation, due to have begun on June 30. They said the new timetable meant they had to renegotiate their existing collective wage agreement.

"Our proposal was to initially maintain the existing wage accord in place for another six months, with the exception of those clauses which could damage the implementation of the 24-hour port," said the CODESP official.
This would mean removing all clauses linked to shifts and timetables, she said.
CODESP had also filed a request with the regional labor tribunal that any new collective wage agreement contain a clause establishing fines for every day lost due to strikes, she said.
CODESP estimates its revenue at 1.2 million reais ($1.1 million) per day and each vessel paralyzed today costs 10,000 to 12,000 reais, the spokeswoman said.
